question: In a triangle MNR, the bisectors of angle MNR and angle MRN are respectively NO and RO, which intersect at O. If angle M=60^circ and angle MRN=66^circ, then the value of angle RON is :
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any triangle, the angle formed by the intersection of the internal angle bisectors is equal to 90° plus half of the third (opposite) angle.

⇒ ∠RON = 90° + (∠M ÷ 2)

⇒ ∠RON = 90° + (60° ÷ 2)

⇒ ∠RON = 90° + 30° = 120°

**∴ The correct answer is 120°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠M = 60°

∠MRN = 66°

**Calculations:**

In ΔMNR, the sum of all three interior angles is always 180°.

⇒ ∠M + ∠MNR + ∠MRN = 180°

⇒ 60° + ∠MNR + 66° = 180°

⇒ ∠MNR + 126° = 180°

⇒ ∠MNR = 180° − 126° = 54°

We are given that NO and RO are the angle bisectors of ∠MNR and ∠MRN respectively.

⇒ ∠ONR = ∠MNR ÷ 2 = 54° ÷ 2 = 27°

⇒ ∠ORN = ∠MRN ÷ 2 = 66° ÷ 2 = 33°

Now, considering the inner triangle ΔONR, the sum of angles must also be 180°.

⇒ ∠RON + ∠ONR + ∠ORN = 180°

⇒ ∠RON + 27° + 33° = 180°

⇒ ∠RON + 60° = 180°

⇒ ∠RON = 180° − 60° = 120°

**∴ The correct answer is 120°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Incenter Angle Property

The angle formed by the intersection of internal angle bisectors of two angles of a triangle is always equal to 90° + (Third Angle ÷ 2).

Excenter Angle Property

The angle formed by the intersection of external angle bisectors of two base angles of a triangle is always equal to 90° − (Third Angle ÷ 2).

Orthocenter Angle Property

The angle formed by the intersection of altitudes inside a triangle is supplementary to the opposite angle. Formula: 180° − Opposite Angle.

Circumcenter Angle Property

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended by it at any remaining part of the circle. Formula: 2 × Opposite Angle.
